authorization: User explicitly requested further improvement iteration after the failed memory study. This is a new study; the old gate and conclusions remain unchanged.
hypothesis: Removing absolute ammo/health/distance inputs may reduce transfer sensitivity; compare with ordinary averaging of the original history models and explicit observable-event gating.

selection.rank: Eligible candidates must meet utility and kill thresholds against rules in both development scenarios. Choose largest minimum net-utility gain across the two scenarios; ties by arm name. Select once; no confirmation fallback.

confirmation_arms: Selected candidate, rules, original-history probability ensemble, rule with event memory, selected head with event memory disabled, and each of five preserved history_MAP policies. Matched seeds, steering, seven-tic windows and costs.
primary: Selected minus rules and selected minus the mean of the five preserved history_MAP fits in each of two scenarios.

confirmation_gate.interval: 99.375% two-sided paired percentile bootstrap, Bonferroni for four utility and four kill comparisons. Resample seeds and history training fits. Exploratory finite-sample evidence, not guaranteed coverage.

secondary: Matched no-rest and command-rest controls identify simpler explanations; kills, ammo used, actual engine reward, truncations, success and firing windows, total decision compute.
claim_boundary: Engineering comparison of feature selection, bagging and event memory. No new algorithm or Bayesian gain claim. Both scenarios used in development; fresh-seed confirmation is not unseen-task validation. Probability ensembles use five training fits, so compare against the original ensemble before attributing a gain to representation. Keep the old failed studies unchanged.
design_evidence: Historical training is Center-only; prior confirmation showed wide between-fit variation. This follow-up is exploratory adaptation to completed studies and uses wholly new development/confirmation seeds.
training: Reuse exactly the five disjoint historical Center training replicates from memory-doom-v1, with the same issued-fire labels. Each ensemble averages the five MAP probabilities. Original ensemble uses preserved 17-feature fits. New current head has four features; new history head has eight. Same Gaussian prior precision 1 and maximum 40 Newton iterations. No new labels or weights selected by confirmation.
portable_features: bias, visible, min(abs_aim/max(.04,.65*half_width),3), half_width; history adds previous issued-fire, previous observed-hit, capped age since issued-fire, has-previous. No absolute ammo, health or distance. This changes representation and dimensionality; it does not isolate each removed feature.
ensemble: Mean sigmoid prediction over five fitted weight vectors, not sigmoid of the mean weights. All ensemble policies receive the same total 80 historical training episodes.
event_gate: A one-window rest following observed ammo decrease or previous hit. Gate also requires visible target; this additional constraint is documented and matched by no-gate ensemble controls. Rule-based steering always retained.
